thread:
michael: Heads-up — we've seen a couple p99 spikes during tenant cold starts this week. Traces point to a bunch of KV prefix misses and then long prefetch stalls that cascade. Thinking we need a more explicit prefetch + staleness-recovery pattern for prefix cache. Anyone have context or strong opinions?

sara: We hit this a while back in eu-prod. My preferred approach: lease-based prefetch so only one worker per prefix does the heavy fetch. Serve stale while prefetching with a short stale window, plus jittered backoff for retries. Keeps latency bounded and avoids thundering herd. :+1:

kevin: Lease approach is fine but watch correctness. If a tenant writes to the keyspace, serving stale KVs can produce incorrect results (read-after-write). We need a way to detect recent writes and either block or revalidate before serving stale.

yun: For the write-detection bit, we used a tiny metadata stamp in front of the prefix: last_write_ts. On lookup if last_write_ts > stale_cutoff then force synchronous fetch. Cheap and effective. Downside: extra metadata read.

michael: Can you paste the config you used?

sara: Sure — here's roughly what we ran in staging:

```
prefetch:
  lease_ttl_ms: 800
  max_concurrent_prefetches_per_shard: 6
  jitter_ms: 120
stale_serve:
  enabled: true
  stale_window_ms: 1000
  max_stale_serves_per_minute_per_tenant: 10
```

sara: Also we had a soft-pin during prefetch: increment residency weight so eviction doesn't immediately drop prefetched pages until owner finishes.

kevin: Soft-pin is fine but needs a bounded cost. If many prefixes get pinned it'll bloat the cache. Suggest pin decay: pin_weight decays after lease release. Also implement a limit on total pinned bytes per shard.

maria: From a metrics/alerting viewpoint we should track: prefetch_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), stale_served_rate, stale_blocked_due_to_recent_write, lease_acquisitions, prefetch_failures. SLA: stale_served_rate < 1% for user-facing routes.

michael: Ops question: what happens when eviction drops a page mid-prefetch? Could lose owner and then two workers race to fetch. We should either bump residency during prefetch or use a heartbeat on lease that prevents eviction.

kevin: Bumping residency is preferable to preventing eviction entirely. Implementation: increment a soft_pin counter at prefetch start, decrement at finish/fail. Eviction respects soft_pin by adding virtual weight. It avoids hard locks.

yun: Minor correctness note: if we serve stale and then apply a fetched delta, we need to ensure output determinism for callers. For some model pipelines, returning stale + later revalidate can cause confusing downstream behavior. We should only serve stale for pure read-only or idempotent paths.

maria: Good call — we can gate stale-serving per route. Add config per-route or per-tenant opt-in. Also add a header/metric indicating response was stale so app owners can filter/tests.

michael: Rollout plan suggestion: default off. Implement feature flag + config. Enable for 10% tenants in canary region, monitor metrics for 48h. If p99 improves and stale_rate < 0.5% and no correctness incidents, expand.

kevin: One more tradeoff: lease TTL vs latency. Short TTL reduces time a single owner holds fetch responsibility but increases lease churn. We need to tune based on observed prefetch durations. Add histogram for lease_hold_time.

sara: For implementation details — owner_id stored in shard-local metadata with CAS. Prefetch path: attempt CAS to become owner -> if success start prefetch + soft_pin -> on finish CAS owner->nil and decrement pin. If CAS fails, read owner and serve stale (if allowed) or tail-wait with jitter.

michael: Sounds actionable. Can we agree on metrics + experiment parameters? Proposed defaults: lease_ttl_ms=800, stale_window_ms=1000, max_concurrent_prefetches=6, pinned_bytes_limit_per_shard=200MB, canary 10% tenants. Target stale_served_rate < 1% and no read-after-write incidents.

maria: I'm capturing metrics: I'll add dashboards for prefetch_latency, stale_served_rate, blocked_by_recent_write, pin_utilization. I'll also add an annotation event during rollout.

deploy-bot: staging rollout of prefetch-spike-detector completed at 2026-03-20T10:22:00Z :rocket:

michael: Action items: (1) kevin/sara spike PR for lease + soft_pin (2) yun add last_write_ts check and optional per-route gating (3) maria dashboard + alerts (4) ops: canary enablement script. I'll file a ticket and assign.

sara: I'll start the spike — will keep it small and put behind a feature flag.

kevin: I'll help with CAS semantics and eviction weight changes.

michael: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the spike results. :thumbsup:
